newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Gold role seen in new European central bank.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Gold role seen in new European central bank.

text.p: Gold is likely to play a role in the new European central banking system, the World Gold Council said on Wednesday.
"Gold will almost certainly have a role in the balance sheet of the new European Central Bank," Robert Pringle, head of the Centre for Public Policy Studies of the WGC said.
Introduction of a Eurpean currency in 1999 will cause the biggest shake-up in reserve currencies in 50 years, and inject uncertainty into the marketplace, Pringle said.

"Given all these circumstances, although it is natural to expect further sales by some central banks, it will be equally natural to expect other official holders to be interested in increasing their gold holdings or in acquiring some gold for the first time," Pringle said.
Both buying and selling of gold by central banks will be conducted discreetly and in a manner to avoid disrupting the international market, he said.
"In the context of further strong jewellery demand, the market can look to the future with confidence despite the prospect of some further official sales," Pringle said.
Official sector reserves of gold have been stable at between 34,000 and 35,000 tonnes for nearly 30 years, Pringle noted.
Highly publicised central banks sales since 1989 have reduced total official gold reserves by less than five percent, he said. "There has been no large-scale move out of gold," Pringle said.
